SMTO-HTTP-0047 — SMTO's web request was set up incorrectly

GUID: 9277da59-e7a6-4c4a-98e3-f7468aa161ec
Slug: http-invalid-request
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The request the task tried to send had a missing or badly formed part, such as the address or a header. SMTO stopped before sending it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel to see which part of the request was rejected. The message names the piece that wasn't accepted.
  2. Run the task again with clearer details: the exact web address, what to send, and whether it should only read or also change something. The Agent builds the request from your instructions, so a missing or unclear piece makes it invalid.
  3. If the task uses a saved connection, open it in Parameter Store, check Base URL and any Default header entries for typos, then save and select Test connection. The same error appears when a saved connection's settings aren't valid.

What success looks like

  • The task's request is sent and gets a reply.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same request again unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP request failed its argument contract, JSON validity or another validation path with no narrower kind, before dispatch.

What this means

  • The HTTP request fails its argument contract, JSON validity or a validation path that has no narrower kind. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The HTTP request fails its argument contract, JSON validity or a validation path that has no narrower kind.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the safe field-level validation detail against the current advertised schema; this generic kind alone does not identify the field.

How to fix it

  • Correct the named fields against the http.request argument schema (url, method, headers, query, body, connection_ref or profile_key); if a saved profile is involved, open it in Parameter Store and correct its fields. The request was not dispatched.
  • Correct the named fields against the advertised native HTTP request schema.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected request validates before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
